The Foundation Stone of this Bridge was laid 12th June 1878, by The Right Honourable William Varey Lord Mayor. John Bellerby, Esquire, Sheriff. George Gordon Page, Esquire, Engineer.

This Bridge was formally declared free from tolls on April 1st 1914 by The Right Hon. Henry Rhodes Brown Lord Mayor. Robert Newbald Ray Esquire, Sheriff. Alderman Norman Green, Chairman of Bridge Committee.
Near to this place, Margaret Clitherow of York, Saint of the Catholic Church, was martyred for her Christian Faith, on 25th March 1586.
Near this place, Robert Aske leader of the Pilgrimage of Grace died for his faith in 1537, martyred by Henry VIII.
Mary Ann Craven 1826-1900 Master Sugar Confectioner established a factory on this site. Later known as Craven’s French Almond Works, it continued here until 1966.

eras.label: Mapped site · auto T1
eras.summary: Location and terrain only. OpenStreetMap has no mapped outline for this site.
eras.basis: Everything drawn is traced from OpenStreetMap ways (ODbL) and the Terrarium elevation tiles. Each element names its OSM way.
eras.conjecture: Walls and buildings without a sourced height are drawn as kerb-high plan lines, never as masses. Closed walls have no gates: none are mapped. The DEM is ~30 m source resolution: it cannot show terraces, ditches or scarps. Nothing historic is depicted.
